problem: Old db6 archives a nonzero auditor faithfully, then asserts timer stop0 even when its already-elapsed transient timer has autoGCed. This aborts before failed retained service cleanup and the final owned-release receipt. The original audit nonzero and every failed archive/stop remain facts.
implementation: New separate source; selected db6, waiter0a1 and original01a6 are unchanged.
Same-process launch→observe only. Successful exact launch timer cat/show plus InvocationID/Unit and sealed archive are required; observe cannot adopt historical output identities.
All six original command records/raw streams keep actual exit or timeout status. original_archive_status and all_six_original_archive_commands_succeeded expose incomplete commands.
Already-absent timer is skipped, not represented as stop0. Timer stop5 is accepted only after exact launch evidence, fresh original preflight and subsequent not-found; its actual5 remains in receipt.
Timer then service actions require exact original invocation/identity or observed absence. Unknown/replaced units are not stopped or reset. Only the authenticated original failed state may be reset.

Incomplete observation/archive/release emits the new final schema with unit_released=false and lifecycle_complete=false, preserving linked partial release records. Successful cleanup never changes original_exit. CLI returns original nonzero audit exit; exit0 requires complete lifecycle.

pin and publish function bodies are byte-identical to db6. The systemd retained Type=exec/RemainAfterExit/Restart=no,3s timer, CUDAhidden/unset environment, first-identity .01s poll and direct payload recipe remain; config is constrained to existing bounded audit fields.

review_risks: No runtime behavior or future test pass is claimed. Root may implement/run these stdlib-faked cases only after campaign release and explicit selection.

systemctl stop/reset is name-based and has no invocation compare-and-swap. Guards query exact identity immediately before each action; root must retain exclusive ownership of its unique audit names across that check/action interval.

If original live PID/start is missed, launch timer evidence is missing, a source/config changes, or an identity is ambiguous, this proposal leaves unresolved units untouched for explicit root handling.
Launch/scheduling failures produce root-launch-error-preserved.json rather than pretending an observed original audit exists. They do not grant owned-release success.
An unexpected terminal signal does not become an ordinary Code1 audit exit; bounded observation remains incomplete and no cleanup is authorized by an invented exit.

The pure metadata control launches only the exact root-approved auditor argv; proving that selected argv/plan/binding/source closure is still a future root/waiter obligation. No quality criteria, error classifier, rows, scorer, cohort timing or installed sources are altered.
